name: Peri-peri chicken livers
summary: Chicken livers seared quickly and simmered in a creamy, garlicky peri-peri tomato sauce, served with crusty Portuguese rolls for dipping.
about: Peri-peri livers are a fixture of Portuguese-South African cafés and family tables, a starter or light meal mopped up with soft-crusted Portuguese rolls. Livers are one of the cheapest proteins in the shop and cook in minutes, which makes this a weeknight standby. Adjust the chilli to suit the table.

ingredients.name: Red bird's-eye chillies
ingredients.note: finely chopped; leave out for a mild sauce

steps: Cut each liver in half at the connecting sinew and trim off any green or stringy bits. Pat them very dry with paper towel so they sear rather than stew.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat until shimmering. Add half the livers in one layer and sear for 1–2 minutes a side until browned outside but still pink inside. Lift onto a plate and repeat with the rest.
Turn the heat to medium, add the butter and onion and fry for 5 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, chillies and paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato paste, peri-peri sauce and Worcestershire sauce and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the cream. Simmer for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens slightly and turns a rosy orange.

Return the livers and their juices and simmer gently for 2–3 minutes, just until they are cooked through but still soft; a cut liver should be barely pink in the centre. Overcooked livers turn grainy.
Stir in the lemon juice, season with salt and scatter with parsley. Serve straight from the pan with warm Portuguese rolls for dipping.
